result.title: DelegateEval: Evaluating Platforms for Personal External Service Agents
result.comment: 28 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Evaluation framework and experimental design
result.summary: AI agents that work for an individual over time may also help that individual serve external clients. We define a personal external service agent as an agent authorized and continuously managed by a specific individual to accept client requests, deliver work, and provide ongoing support using that person's knowledge, experience, professional methods, and service boundaries. Such agents could allow individuals to serve more clients with less direct involvement and generate economic value at scale. We propose DelegateEval, a platform-level evaluation framework for agent systems that may combine large language models, reusable skills, protocols such as MCP, and executable tool environments. It covers eight dimensions: ease of creation, service discovery and matching, delivery quality, expertise inheritance, service continuity, learning and improvement, reliability and governance, and efficiency and value. These dimensions assess whether a platform enables people with different backgrounds to turn their expertise into ongoing services that deliver verifiable work, develop capabilities through experience, and remain economically feasible. We present the framework and an experimental design. Complete datasets, executable environments, a unified scoring protocol, and cross-model results remain to be developed and empirically validated.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DelegateEval，一个面向「个人对外服务型智能体」的平台级评测框架，从创建便捷性、服务匹配、交付质量、专长继承、服务连续性、学习改进、可靠治理与效率价值八个维度评估平台能力，并给出实验设计。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文侧重智能体平台的商业可行性与服务交付评测，未涉及视觉或多模态内部表示、latent 推理状态生成与使用、THINK/LOOK/STOP 等决策机制，也未给出可供迁移的具体状态或训练方法线索，与 LVR 主线缺少实质联系。
